name: Ceigall India Ltd
tagline: ~Rs 5,900 Cr roads / highways EPC contractor (structures, elevated corridors, tunnels, metro) with a Rs 18,554 Cr order book (~4.6x revenue) and ~25% ROCE - strong execution and visibility, but a low-multiple sector, HAM equity drag and mid-cap size keep it out of a 10x/100x thesis
business_overview: Ceigall India Ltd (NSE: CEIGALL, IPO August 2024), 20+ years in infrastructure EPC - highways, expressways, flyovers, tunnels, elevated roads and metro rail - executing EPC, HAM, DBFOT and now renewable-linked projects. Founder-promoter led (Singla family), Punjab-headquartered.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 18,554 Cr - ~4.6x FY26 revenue (19 EPC, 10 HAM, 1 DBFOT, 7 renewable projects)
~Rs 11,332 Cr vs ~Rs 5,000 Cr guidance (~35% from renewables)
fundamentals_narrative: Ceigall executes well - ~25% ROCE, Q4FY26 revenue +37% with PAT +~75% and operating margin up to ~16%, and an order book of ~Rs 18,554 Cr that is ~4.6x FY26 revenue, built on FY26 inflows (~Rs 11,332 Cr) that more than doubled the ~Rs 5,000 Cr guidance. Full-year FY26 revenue growth was a modest ~17%, so order-book-to-revenue conversion has been the constraint. The structural issues are sector-wide: roads EPC trades at low-teens P/E, HAM projects tie up sponsor equity and depress consolidated returns/cash flow, and receivables/retention are heavy. At ~Rs 5,927 Cr the company is already a genuine mid-cap; a 10x implies ~Rs 59,000 Cr and 100x-in-10-years is not credible for a roads EPC. The order book supports several years of growth, but not a re-rating of the kind a 10x thesis needs.

value_chain.note: Roads infra is not a listed active theme. Order visibility is strong, but the value chain here has no pricing-power node - awards are competitively bid, HAM equity drags consolidated returns, and the market prices the whole cohort at low-teens P/E.

verdict_headline: Well-run roads EPC with an exceptional order book, but a low-multiple sector, HAM equity drag and mid-cap size make it 'neither'; conviction Medium
verdict_reasoning: Sovrenn-news seed (tier 4.65). The Sovrenn trigger (Q4FY26 +37% sales / +79% PAT, OPM 13% -> 16%) holds up and the ~Rs 18,554 Cr order book (~4.6x revenue) is genuinely strong.

But this is a genuine mid-cap (~Rs 5,927 Cr) in a structurally low-multiple sector: roads EPC trades at low-teens P/E, HAM equity commitments drag consolidated returns and cash flow, and FY26 revenue grew only ~17% despite the order book. There is no named structural inflection - it is a good contractor executing a strong pipeline. Per the large-cap / mid-cap rule this is 'neither' on size and sector math.

No live-theme match (roads infra is not a listed theme; the renewable civil work is adjacent to priority-2 at most). No red flag. conviction Medium (execution quality and order visibility are real); thesis_fit 'neither'; revisit_after_30d false.
